summary: Template adoption telemetry header rejected by some corporate proxies (HTTP 400/431) — request never reaches Redwood
content:
Customer reports that requests from the RAG+Agent Quickstart template fail only when routed through their corporate proxy. Proxy rejects "unknown" request headers; as a result the HTTP request never reaches Redwood (no request-id, no gateway logs).

Issue summary
- When using the Quickstart template defaults (telemetry tagging enabled), requests include one or more template-origin telemetry headers.
- Northbridge’s corporate proxy rejects requests containing unapproved custom headers, returning HTTP 400/431 before the request leaves their network.
- Removing the custom header(s) makes requests succeed immediately.

Impact
- Blocks template evaluation behind corporate network controls.
- Customer perception: Redwood API is down/unreliable (but failures occur upstream of Redwood).
- Limits our ability to use header-based adoption telemetry in enterprise environments.

Environment
- Customer network: corporate proxy with strict header allowlist (exact vendor not disclosed)
- Client: Python quickstart template (internal beta branch per customer)
- Redwood: Hosted API, prod, us-east

Steps to reproduce (customer)
1) Run template behind corporate proxy (HTTPS interception disabled; standard outbound proxy).
2) Execute template endpoint that triggers LLM call.
3) Observe proxy error: request rejected due to custom header.
4) Manually remove telemetry header(s) and retry.
5) Request succeeds.

Expected
- Template should work behind common enterprise proxies with default configuration.
- Telemetry tagging should not break baseline API calls.

Actual
- Proxy rejects request when template telemetry headers are present. Request never reaches Redwood gateway.

Evidence / logs (sanitized)
- Customer proxy response (reported):
  - Status: 431 Request Header Fields Too Large (sometimes 400 Bad Request)
  - Error text: "Request rejected: header not allowed" / "Unknown header: X-Redwood-Template" (wording varies)
- Redwood side:
  - No corresponding gateway request logs for the timestamp window.
  - No request-id returned.

Investigation notes
- Correlated with internal Slack incident-adjacent thread about telemetry headers causing 4xx in some proxies (see #incidents reference shared by Support).
- This is not a Redwood API failure; it’s a compatibility issue with our telemetry mechanism.
- Header approach is convenient for downstream filtering but fragile with strict proxy/header policies.

Workaround (provided to customer)
- Disable template telemetry headers and rely on standard SDK headers only.
- Template-level change: make telemetry opt-in instead of opt-out.

Decision / resolution
- Decision (DevEx + PM + Gateway): make template-origin telemetry tagging opt-in.
  - Default templates will NOT send template telemetry headers unless explicitly enabled.
  - For customers who want to participate, provide a clear env var toggle and docs section (privacy + compatibility note).
- Gateway will continue to allow/validate a small set of telemetry headers (for opt-in users), but templates should not emit them by default.

Customer-facing guidance (final)
- Set template telemetry to disabled (default in upcoming template release). For current version, remove/disable the header injection.
- If customer later wants telemetry tagging for internal KPIs, coordinate with network/security to allowlist the header(s) or use a non-header mechanism (future enhancement).

Follow-ups
- DevEx: Update Python + TypeScript templates to make telemetry tagging opt-in and document proxy compatibility note.
- Docs: Add troubleshooting entry: "Corporate proxy rejects unknown headers" with fix steps.
- Telemetry/PM: Confirm KPIs still measurable for self-serve users; enterprise adoption metrics may be undercounted by design.

---
Comments / timeline

2025-03-06 09:18 (Priya Shah, Support)
Customer reports 400/431 from corporate proxy when running RAG template. Removing template telemetry header makes it work. Asking Eng whether we can avoid non-standard headers by default.

2025-03-06 10:02 (Owen Phillips, Support)
Confirmed no gateway logs for customer timestamps. Likely request never reaches Redwood. Requested sanitized proxy error message and the exact header name(s) being flagged.

2025-03-06 11:11 (Northbridge Financial)
Proxy blocks unknown headers. The header flagged is "X-Redwood-Template" (exact case may differ). When removed, calls succeed.

2025-03-06 12:30 (Brian Murphy, Eng - API Ergonomics)
If proxy blocks unknown headers, this will keep happening. We can whitelist on our gateway but can’t force customer proxy behavior. Recommendation: make templates not send these headers by default; keep as opt-in.

2025-03-07 09:05 (Monica Patel, DevEx)
Agree. Templates should be production-minded by default; telemetry must not be a footgun. We’ll change default to off and add an env var toggle.

2025-03-07 14:22 (Priya Shah, Support)
Shared workaround with customer: remove template telemetry header injection; continue with standard SDK. Customer unblocked.

2025-03-10 16:40 (Brian Murphy, Eng)
Noted related gateway work to validate/pass a small allowlist of telemetry headers for opt-in usage. Also aligning with DevEx on naming and keeping cardinality low.

2025-03-11 10:15 (Priya Shah, Support)
Closing as resolved: customer has workaround, and product decision made to ship opt-in telemetry in templates + docs update. Tracking template change in DevEx queue and will reference in release notes.

Resolution
- Workaround provided and verified by customer.
- Product decision: telemetry headers from templates will be opt-in going forward to avoid corporate proxy incompatibilities.

Support closure notes
- If customer wants adoption telemetry tagging later, advise them to allowlist the exact header(s) with their proxy/security team, or wait for future non-header tagging approach if shipped.
- If they still see 4xx with headers removed, reopen with request-id + timestamp + region so we can check gateway/serving logs.
